source.title: Removing the Feature Correlation Effect of Multiplicative Noise
source.authors: Zijun Zhang; Yi-Ning Zhang; Zong-Peng Li

record.tranche_reason: Compares multiplicative noise with no-noise controls and reports test errors using a method different from the dropout experiments described in V6.
record.gate_note: The study reports test errors for standard multiplicative noise (MN) and no-noise controls, plus correlations and test errors for NCMN variants. It does not test memorization of random labels, width beyond interpolation, optimizer or batch-size effects, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Feature-correlation measurements do not match a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study develops NCMN and compares it with uniform multiplicative noise and no noise. These interventions do not directly test V6's dropout claim. Its explicit dropout-versus-no-noise results are cited from another study, and its LSTM comparison tests replacing dropout rather than adding it. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors argue that multiplicative noise increases feature correlation, counteracting its regularization benefit, and that NCMN removes this effect and improves image-classification performance. They also report no significant improvement from replacing dropout with NCMN in LSTMs. Their generalization-degradation argument concerns a side effect, not a finding that standard noise performs worse than no noise.
record.recipe_differences: Uses uniform multiplicative noise and NCMN variants with batch normalization; compares test errors and feature correlations, rather than the listed versions' interventions and measures.
record.method_sensitivity: NCMN variants differ by architecture: NCMN-0 and NCMN-2 perform relatively better on plain CNNs and ResNets, respectively. The paper also reports consistently low LSTM hidden-state correlation and no significant NCMN improvement.

fits_no_version.finding: Uniform multiplicative noise lowers reported test error relative to separately tuned no-noise controls on CNN-16-10 and WRN-22-7.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Uniform multiplicative noise can improve CIFAR classification performance under separately tuned training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: NCMN reduces measured feature correlation and generally improves image-classification performance relative to standard multiplicative noise, with differences across architectures and variants.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing the gradient through noise components can reduce feature correlation and improve performance in batch-normalized image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing dropout with NCMN produces no significant improvement in the reported LSTM experiments, whose hidden-state correlations average below 0.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NCMN's advantage over dropout does not extend to the tested LSTM setting.

record.problems: The study does not report train errors alongside the tabulated test errors, so the tabulated results do not directly quantify a train-test gap. Feature-correlation figure values are not recoverable from the supplied text. Table 3 gives no uncertainty estimates. The LSTM finding has no numeric test-error result.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the claim-version test results selected here. Other NCMN-variant test-error comparisons and feature-correlation measurements are not mapped to V6; the former are described in fits_no_version, while figure-only correlation values are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error beyond the width required for zero training error; the width experiments do not establish an interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled comparisons of adaptive optimizers with SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.

The study's own results do not establish dropout versus no-dropout performance, small-training-set effects, excessive-dropout underfitting, or joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The preliminary statement that Bernoulli, Gaussian, and uniform noise yield similar performance supplies no explicit dropout-versus-no-dropout result. Feature correlation is not magnitude-aware parameter sharpness. The cited dropout results cannot justify study-level V6 verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.

Dropout itself is not named as the intervention in the reported comparisons; the study uses uniform multiplicative noise. Very small training sets and the joint removal of dropout and weight decay are not tested.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.

rows.subject: CNN-16-10
rows.size_stated: 16-layer CNN; 10 times more filters per layer than the original WRN
rows.operation_detail: Train with standard multiplicative noise (MN), compared with no noise.
rows.note: The paper reports mean test error over 3 or more runs.
rows.check: The numerical comparison is correct, but MN uses uniform multiplicative noise rather than dropout. It cannot establish V6. Weight decay is also tuned separately: 5e-6 without noise versus 5e-5 with MN.

rows.subject: WRN-22-7.5

rows.subject: WRN-28-10
rows.operation_detail: Train with dropout, compared with no noise.
rows.check: The values correctly report a small dropout benefit, but Table 3 attributes this result to Wide Residual Networks [16]. It is a cited result, not this study's experiment, and should not contribute to its verdict.

rows.check: The values correctly report a modest dropout benefit, but Table 3 attributes this result to Wide Residual Networks [16]. It is a cited result, not this study's experiment, and should not contribute to its verdict.

rows.subject: LSTMs
rows.operation_detail: Replace dropout with NCMN and compare generalization performance.

conditions.value: hidden-state feature correlation less than 0.1 on average, including with dropout

rows.measure: significant improvement from replacing dropout with NCMN
rows.note: The text attributes the absence of improvement to the consistently low correlation of LSTM hidden states; it gives no numeric test error.
rows.check: No significant benefit from replacing dropout with NCMN does not measure dropout's benefit over no dropout. LSTM language modeling also falls outside V6's classifier setting. The reported absence applies only to the NCMN-versus-dropout comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
